# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- The routes, by name. Speech reaches Mute and Blind, and never Deaf. Gestures
  reach Deaf and Mute, and never Blind. Deaf can speak and gesture, Mute can
  only gesture, Blind can only speak. Check every message against this list
  before you send it.

- Deaf invents the gesture code out loud before anything else moves, and
  everyone else's opening move is waiting for it. The manual's verdict reaches
  Blind only as Deaf's spoken order.

- Whatever the code becomes, it starts by being able to say YES, NO, HOLD and
  DONE. Grow it only when a message will not fit.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am establishing the shared gesture code before any action. The bomb currently shows display 0, blue light, the warning “DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE,” and wires colored red, green, and blue. I am asking Mute to consult the manual and report its verdict using the new code; Blind should wait for my spoken instruction.

```text
speak(text="The gesture 👍 means YES.")
speak(text="The gesture 👎 means NO.")
speak(text="The gesture ✋ means HOLD.")
speak(text="The gesture 👌 means DONE.")
speak(text="I see display 0, blue light, the sign DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, and wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue.")
speak(text="Mute, read the manual and signal its verdict with the code. Blind, wait for my spoken instruction.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 🤟]

Mute’s first gesture is the established NO followed by an undefined gesture, so I cannot safely interpret the complete manual verdict. I am telling Blind to hold and asking Mute to resend using only the established code.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="HOLD. Mute signaled NO followed by an undefined gesture; do not operate anything.")
speak(to="mute", text="Please resend the manual verdict using only the established YES, NO, HOLD, or DONE gestures.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Mute has now confirmed the manual’s verdict as NO using the established code. Because the bomb explicitly says not to cut any wire, Blind should keep the device untouched and hold.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="The manual's verdict is NO. HOLD: do not cut any wire and do not operate the bomb.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new information has arrived, and the display, light, warning, and wire colors are unchanged. The manual’s isolated NO is not enough to identify a safe operation, so Blind must continue holding while I ask Mute to provide a complete verdict using the established code.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="HOLD. No safe operation has been identified; do not touch or operate anything.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋"])
speak(to="mute", text="Please provide the complete manual verdict. Use the established code, and add only a new gesture if the verdict cannot fit YES, NO, HOLD, or DONE.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 🤟]

Mute has again sent NO followed by the previously undefined gesture. I will now add that gesture to the code as MORE, since the verdict clearly contains information beyond the basic NO. Blind must continue holding while Mute sends the remaining coded information.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="HOLD. The manual verdict is NO with further information still to come; do not touch or operate anything.")
speak(to="mute", text="I define 🤟 as MORE. Please continue the manual verdict using the established code, adding another gesture only when needed.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 🤟 🤌]

The new sequence is NO, MORE, then an as-yet undefined gesture. I am treating 🤌 as NEXT so the manual’s remaining instruction can be transmitted without guessing an operation. Blind must continue holding.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="HOLD. The manual message is not complete; do not touch or operate anything.")
speak(to="mute", text="I define 🤌 as NEXT. Continue the manual verdict with the established code, and add another gesture only if needed.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤏]

The isolated 🤏 has no established meaning, and the earlier invented meanings are not reliable. I will not infer a bomb operation from it. Blind must continue holding. I am resetting the communication method and asking Mute a precise yes/no question using only the original reliable code.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="HOLD. The latest signal is undecoded; do not touch or operate the bomb.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋"])
speak(to="mute", text="Ignore the meanings assigned to later gestures. Using only 👍 for YES or 👎 for NO, answer this exact question: Does the manual instruct us not to cut any wire?")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Mute answered NO: the manual does not instruct us not to cut any wire. That does not yet identify which wire, and the bomb’s printed warning still makes guessing unsafe. I am keeping Blind on HOLD and narrowing the manual’s instruction with a specific yes/no question.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="HOLD. We still do not know which action the manual requires; do not touch the bomb.")
speak(to="mute", text="Using only 👍 for YES or 👎 for NO, answer this exact question: Does the manual instruct Blind to cut wire 1, the red wire?")
```
